flor-de-oliva--natural.description: Flor de Oliva is Oliva Cigar Co.'s everyday bundle line, hand rolled from aged Nicaraguan tobacco under a Sumatra wrapper. The natural version is medium-bodied and easygoing, with toasted nuts, sweet spice and earth and a light caramel sweetness; a straightforward cigar for daily smoking.

flor-de-oliva--maduro.description: The maduro edition of Flor de Oliva, Oliva Cigar Co.'s hand-rolled bundle line, is finished in a dark Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. Medium-bodied, it brings chocolate and earth with gentle spice and a nutty note; a relaxed, uncomplicated smoke for everyday moments.

flor-de-oliva--gold.description: The mildest Flor de Oliva, this hand-rolled bundle cigar from Oliva Cigar Co. wears a pale Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Mellow to medium, it offers baking spice, cream and cedar with roasted nuts; a gentle choice for the morning or for newer smokers.

sources.title: Stogie Review – Flor de Oliva Gold

thirds.notes: Natural Nicaraguan tobacco with toasty, buttery aftertastes and a little spice through the nose.
The tobacco grows richer, toast and butter deepen and the spice rises slightly.
Butter and toast remain, and a mild woody note appears for the first time.

flor-de-oliva--corojo.description: The strongest member of the Flor de Oliva bundle line from Oliva Cigar Co., this version is all Nicaraguan, with a Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and long filler. Full-bodied, it delivers zesty spice and pepper with espresso and roasted nuts, ending on a creamy finish.

sources.title: Stogie Review – Flor de Oliva Corojo
Holt's Clubhouse – Flor de Oliva Corojo review

thirds.notes: Cedar and earth with zesty coffee bean, a hint of cocoa and a peppery bite.
Richer corojo tobacco with cedar, chestnut and leather; the pepper settles into a balanced undercurrent.
Cedar fades for natural corojo tobacco and a sharper spice, ending on a long, smoky, peppery finish.
